title: One command-response exchange per connection
summary: Queue Transport intentionally uses one delivery or probe request per TCP connection. This gives simple reconnect/failure boundaries and means each derived directional nonce is consumed once in the current protocol design.
invariants: The session-nonce safety argument depends on the one-command/response-per-connection lifecycle.
Store-and-forward and retry remain channel responsibilities, not an excuse to keep a socket session open indefinitely.
Changing to multiple commands per session would require a new nonce/sequence construction and fresh qualification; do not merely loop the current secure-frame code.

provenance.claim: README states one delivery per TCP connection, bounded framing, authentication and fresh-connection idempotence.
Documentation ties once-per-direction nonce use to one command/response per TCP connection.
